confidence_note: Mall-smile scene, partners who "should know", love-and-change point and the remedy are from LitCharts chapter summary and direct Ruiz quotations (PhilosophersNotes); not checked against the book text. Old text dropped: the migraine partner story and "relationships are mostly built on assumptions".
facts: Ruiz: we make assumptions about everything and believe them true, could swear they are real.

Scene: you see someone you like at the mall; the person smiles; you assume they like you, picture a relationship, may fantasize about the wedding; we do this all the time; it gives too much power to an invented reality.
We expect partners to know what we think and want; assume friends and family know us so well we need not communicate; then resent them.
Early in a relationship we see what we like, overlook the rest, assume we can change it; real love is accepting someone as they are; if someone wants to change you, they do not really love you.
Chain: assume, take it personally, blame, send emotional poison with the word; misunderstand and create a big drama for nothing.
We also make assumptions about ourselves because we do not ask questions.
Remedy: ask questions, make sure communication is clear, have the courage to ask until as clear as you can be.
tension: A smile becomes a relationship in seconds, with no word exchanged.

lessons.idea: Fill a gap with a question instead of a guess.
lessons.anchor: The person smiling at the mall is someone you know nothing about.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A manager gets a one-word reply to her draft and asks which part worked.

reflect_final: Which silence or short reply are you filling this week with a guess, when one question to the person would settle it?

use_cases.situation: A partner is quiet at dinner.
use_cases.move: Ask if something is on their mind or they are tired.
Name the assumption and ask directly.

pocket_idea: Turn a guess into one question.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: In Ruiz's example, a smile at the mall is enough to build a whole relationship in your head.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Ruiz describes a smile at the mall that you read as love, down to the wedding. Assumptions grow into misunderstanding and drama for nothing. His fix: ask until you are clear.
